turns.content: Hi, I'm working on an article about child and maternal health in Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh. Could you help me find some clear, reliable data on recent health outcomes in these countries?

**Summary (using latest available data)**  
All three countries have made big gains in child and maternal health, but levels differ sharply: Sri Lanka is near high‑income outcomes, while Nepal and Bangladesh still face significantly higher mortality but very high immunization coverage.

---

## Data

### 1. Under‑5 mortality (per 1,000 live births, WDI)

Latest year: 2023

| Country      | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 (latest) |
|-------------|------|------|------|------|----------------|
| Bangladesh  | <claim id="8a9e83ee" policy="auto">32.4</claim> | <claim id="fd35adfa" policy="auto">31.5</claim> | <claim id="b06ab16a" policy="auto">31</claim> | <claim id="1a2fc2b8" policy="auto">30.7</claim> | <claim id="255dc075" policy="auto">30.6</claim> |
| Nepal       | <claim id="897c41f8" policy="auto">31.4</claim> | <claim id="2e012bfe" policy="auto">29.9</claim> | <claim id="bf07fec7" policy="auto">28.6</claim> | <claim id="4f249b83" policy="auto">27.5</claim> | <claim id="3a010449" policy="auto">26.5</claim> |
| Sri Lanka   | <claim id="0702a648" policy="auto">7.2</claim>  | <claim id="911fe354" policy="auto">6.9</claim>  | <claim id="df8943fa" policy="auto">6.6</claim>  | <claim id="83393ff5" policy="auto">6.4</claim>  | <claim id="a620014b" policy="auto">6.1</claim>  |

Unit: deaths per 1,000 live births.

---

### 2. Neonatal mortality (per 1,000 live births, WDI)

Latest year: 2023

| Country      | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 (latest) |
|-------------|------|------|------|------|----------------|
| Bangladesh  | <claim id="80405380" policy="auto">19.3</claim> | <claim id="4d758c0a" policy="auto">18.7</claim> | <claim id="7cb2678e" policy="auto">18.3</claim> | <claim id="dd6b3363" policy="auto">18</claim>   | <claim id="3b4ace73" policy="auto">17.9</claim> |
| Nepal       | <claim id="19472451" policy="auto">19.5</claim> | <claim id="5d233bca" policy="auto">18.7</claim> | <claim id="ef8a76c7" policy="auto">17.9</claim> | <claim id="e54ca97d" policy="auto">17.2</claim> | <claim id="337c8e30" policy="auto">16.6</claim> |
| Sri Lanka   | <claim id="faff7a9d" policy="auto">4.8</claim>  | <claim id="0febf1ad" policy="auto">4.6</claim>  | <claim id="66a2f91f" policy="auto">4.5</claim>  | <claim id="746983e1" policy="auto">4.3</claim>  | <claim id="26c50c32" policy="auto">4.1</claim>  |

---

### 3. Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births, WDI, modeled)

Latest year: 2023

| Country      | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 (latest) |
|-------------|------|------|------|------|----------------|
| Bangladesh  | <claim id="170ceaa8" policy="auto">157</claim> | <claim id="734404cd" policy="auto">152</claim> | <claim id="ee3e4d22" policy="auto">194</claim> | <claim id="ebaec7a2" policy="auto">131</claim> | <claim id="58c9147c" policy="auto">115</claim> |
| Nepal       | <claim id="cf136c8f" policy="auto">170</claim> | <claim id="b2cd902a" policy="auto">153</claim> | <claim id="e2532961" policy="auto">173</claim> | <claim id="c3b4761f" policy="auto">139</claim> | <claim id="4f348921" policy="auto">142</claim> |
| Sri Lanka   | <claim id="bd4e0fa4" policy="auto">20</claim>  | <claim id="505721d0" policy="auto">23</claim>  | <claim id="6d5bc334" policy="auto">34</claim>  | <claim id="da4bd382" policy="auto">22</claim>  | <claim id="bf8e9daa" policy="auto">18</claim>  |

Unit: maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. (These are modeled WHO/UN estimates, so year‑to‑year bumps can reflect revised data/methods as well as real changes.)

---

### 4. Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total, WB_HNP)

Latest non‑null year in this pull: 2019

| Country      | 2019 (latest available here) |
|-------------|------------------------------|
| Bangladesh  | <claim id="61c90145" policy="auto">59</claim>% |
| Nepal       | <claim id="22b55eaa" policy="auto">77.2</claim>% |
| Sri Lanka   | Data in this query are null for 2019–2023 (Sri Lanka is known from other sources to be very high, but I can’t quote a number from this dataset).

(2020–2023 entries exist but with `OBS_STATUS="O"` and `OBS_VALUE="null"`, so they’re effectively missing in this API slice.)

| Nepal       | <claim id="127c3af7" policy="auto">92</claim>% | <claim id="2480b095" policy="auto">87</claim>% | <claim id="8b27b788" policy="auto">90</claim>% | <claim id="0bf49206" policy="auto">90</claim>% | <claim id="9bc464db" policy="auto">93</claim>% | <claim id="247b35d2" policy="auto">97</claim>% |
| Sri Lanka   | <claim id="e5ca6286" policy="auto">99</claim>% | <claim id="3cf5a415" policy="auto">96</claim>% | <claim id="c2a4b7d8" policy="auto">97</claim>% | <claim id="92232f67" policy="auto">99</claim>% | <claim id="5b42ce22" policy="auto">99</claim>% | <claim id="383e550b" policy="auto">99</claim>% |

---

### 6. Immunization – DPT (% of children 12–23 months, WDI)

Latest year: 2024

| Country      | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 (latest) |
|-------------|------|------|------|------|------|----------------|
| Bangladesh  | <claim id="649d237c" policy="auto">98</claim>% | <claim id="bda2e5ef" policy="auto">97</claim>% | <claim id="74c304aa" policy="auto">97</claim>% | <claim id="f4102124" policy="auto">97</claim>% | <claim id="3d71c061" policy="auto">97</claim>% | <claim id="90f65036" policy="auto">97</claim>% |
| Nepal       | <claim id="b477644f" policy="auto">93</claim>% | <claim id="ecea0b3d" policy="auto">84</claim>% | <claim id="2d2ce930" policy="auto">91</claim>% | <claim id="9acf3e36" policy="auto">90</claim>% | <claim id="8f6d1553" policy="auto">94</claim>% | <claim id="7bbb929c" policy="auto">97</claim>% |
| Sri Lanka   | <claim id="74f1ceb6" policy="auto">99</claim>% | <claim id="adce0825" policy="auto">96</claim>% | <claim id="64afe960" policy="auto">96</claim>% | <claim id="342871df" policy="auto">98</claim>% | <claim id="ca796212" policy="auto">99</claim>% | <claim id="b7aa4f74" policy="auto">97</claim>% |

---

## Analysis (how you might frame this in your article)

- **Child survival has improved, but gaps remain.**  
  - In 2023, under‑5 mortality was about <claim id="255dc075" policy="auto">30.6</claim> per 1,000 in Bangladesh, <claim id="3a010449" policy="auto">26.5</claim> in Nepal, and only <claim id="a620014b" policy="auto">6.1</claim> in Sri Lanka.  
  - Neonatal deaths make up a large share of child mortality in Nepal and Bangladesh (2023 neonatal rates of <claim id="337c8e30" policy="auto">16.6</claim> and <claim id="3b4ace73" policy="auto">17.9</claim> per 1,000, respectively), pointing to issues around birth care and the first month of life.

- **Sri Lanka stands out as a regional leader.**  
  - Under‑5 mortality of <claim id="a620014b" policy="auto">6.1</claim> and maternal mortality of just <claim id="bf8e9daa" policy="auto">18</claim> per 100,000 live births in 2023 place Sri Lanka close to many high‑income countries.  
  - Neonatal mortality is also low at <claim id="26c50c32" policy="auto">4.1</claim> per 1,000 in 2023.

- **Maternal mortality has fallen, but is still high in Nepal and Bangladesh.**  
  - In 2023, Bangladesh’s maternal mortality ratio was <claim id="58c9147c" policy="auto">115</claim> per 100,000, and Nepal’s was <claim id="4f348921" policy="auto">142</claim>, compared to Sri Lanka’s <claim id="bf8e9daa" policy="auto">18</claim>.  
  - Both Nepal and Bangladesh saw substantial declines since 2019 (e.g., Bangladesh from <claim id="170ceaa8" policy="auto">157</claim> to <claim id="58c9147c" policy="auto">115</claim>), but they remain well above SDG targets.

- **Skilled birth attendance is improving but uneven.**  
  - From this dataset, the latest figure for Nepal (2019) shows about <claim id="22b55eaa" policy="auto">77.2</claim>% of births attended by skilled staff, versus <claim id="61c90145" policy="auto">59</claim>% in Bangladesh.  
  - More recent years are missing in this API slice; you may want to cross‑check with DHS/MICS or WHO country profiles for updated national survey estimates, especially for Sri Lanka where we know coverage is very high but don’t have a number here.

- **Immunization coverage is a major success story.**  
  - Measles vaccination in 2024 reached <claim id="247b35d2" policy="auto">97</claim>% in Nepal, <claim id="f80605f0" policy="auto">96</claim>% in Bangladesh, and <claim id="383e550b" policy="auto">99</claim>% in Sri Lanka.  
  - DPT coverage in 2024 was similarly high: <claim id="7bbb929c" policy="auto">97</claim>% in Nepal, <claim id="90f65036" policy="auto">97</claim>% in Bangladesh, and <claim id="b7aa4f74" policy="auto">97</claim>% in Sri Lanka.  
  - These levels help explain why under‑5 mortality has fallen so much despite limited resources, especially in Nepal and Bangladesh.

- **COVID‑era resilience.**  
  - None of the three countries show a dramatic collapse in child immunization coverage in 2020–2021 in these data (there are small dips, e.g., Nepal’s measles coverage dropping to <claim id="2480b095" policy="auto">87</claim>% in 2020, then recovering).  
  - Under‑5 and neonatal mortality continue a gradual downward trend through 2023, suggesting systems were strained but did not break.

---

## Sources

- **World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)**  
  - *Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)* — `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`  
  - *Mortality rate, neonatal (per 1,000 live births)* — `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_NMRT`  
  - *Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)* — `WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`  
  - *Immunization, measles (% of children ages 12–23 months)* — `WB_WDI_SH_IMM_MEAS`  
  - *Immunization, DPT (% of children ages 12–23 months)* — `WB_WDI_SH_IMM_IDPT`

- **World Bank — Health, Nutrition and Population Statistics (HNP)**  
  - *Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total)* — `WB_HNP_SH_STA_BRTC_ZS` (only 2019 non‑null in this pull for Nepal and Bangladesh)

**Limitations:**  
- Maternal mortality and some child mortality figures are modeled estimates, especially for recent years. They are best used for trends and comparisons, not as precise counts.  
- Skilled birth attendance data here are incomplete after 2019; for a detailed article section on delivery care, supplement with DHS/MICS or WHO country profiles.

---

**Suggested follow‑ups:**

1. Can you help me turn these trends into one or two simple comparison charts for the article?  
2. Could you add data on nutrition (stunting, wasting) for children in Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh to round out the picture?  
3. Can you help me pull time‑series data back to 2000 to show the long‑term decline in child and maternal mortality in these three countries?

- **Intent:** Provide clear, recent, comparable child and maternal health statistics for Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, suitable for a narrative article.

    - Under‑5 mortality: `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`
    - Neonatal mortality: `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_NMRT`
    - Maternal mortality ratio (modeled): `WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`

    - Immunization, measles: `WB_WDI_SH_IMM_MEAS`

  - Pulled data for Nepal (NPL), Sri Lanka (LKA), and Bangladesh (BGD) for 2019–2024 (where available) to give you a “recent” window and trends around COVID.

- **Data Gaps:**

  - Other indicators have good annual coverage through 2023, and immunization goes through 2024.

turns.content: I'm working in Python with matplotlib; could you provide a code snippet to create this small multiples chart layout?

Here’s a minimal, ready‑to-adapt `matplotlib` example that builds the 2×3 small‑multiples layout from hard‑coded values for 2019–2023.

You can replace the numbers with your own data structure if needed.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data (2019–2023)
# -----------------------------
years = [2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023]

# Under-5 mortality (per 1,000 live births)
u5 = {
    "Nepal":       [31.4, 29.9, 28.6, 27.5, 26.5],  # WDI_SH_DYN_MORT
    "Bangladesh":  [32.4, 31.5, 31.0, 30.7, 30.6],
    "Sri Lanka":   [7.2,  6.9,  6.6,  6.4,  6.1],
}

# Maternal mortality (per 100,000 live births)
mmr = {
    "Nepal":       [170, 153, 173, 139, 142],       # WDI_SH_STA_MMRT
    "Bangladesh":  [157, 152, 194, 131, 115],
    "Sri Lanka":   [20,  23,  34,  22,  18],
}

countries = ["Nepal", "Bangladesh", "Sri Lanka"]

# -----------------------------
# 2. Figure and axes: 2 rows × 3 columns
# -----------------------------
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    nrows=2, ncols=3,
    figsize=(12, 6),  # adjust as needed for publication
    sharex=True
)

# Row 0: Under-5 mortality
# Row 1: Maternal mortality

for col, country in enumerate(countries):
    # --- Top row: Under-5 mortality ---
    ax_u5 = axes[0, col]
    ax_u5.plot(years, u5[country], marker='o', color='tab:blue')
    ax_u5.set_title(country, fontsize=11)
    ax_u5.set_ylabel("Under-5\n(per 1,000)", fontsize=9)
    ax_u5.grid(alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

    # --- Bottom row: Maternal mortality ---
    ax_mmr = axes[1, col]
    ax_mmr.plot(years, mmr[country], marker='o', color='tab:red')
    ax_mmr.set_ylabel("Maternal\n(per 100,000)", fontsize=9)
    ax_mmr.grid(alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

    # X-axis shared; set only on bottom row
    ax_mmr.set_xticks(years)
    ax_mmr.set_xticklabels(years, rotation=45)

# -----------------------------
# 3. Overall figure formatting
# -----------------------------
fig.suptitle(
    "Under-5 and Maternal Mortality in Nepal, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka (2019–2023)",
    fontsize=13, y=0.98
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])  # leave space for suptitle
plt.show()
```
